title: Til: Ancient Til Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: An evergreen laurel of the Atlantic fog forest. Madeira's Fanal grove was standing when the Portuguese arrived in 1419; Bucaco's til is 38 metres tall.
intro: Til, Ocotea foetens, is an evergreen laurel of the laurisilva, the fog forest that survives today on Madeira, the Canary Islands and a handful of other Atlantic islands. On Madeira's Paul da Serra plateau, the til grove of Fanal was already standing when the Portuguese found the island uninhabited in 1419. One twisted, moss-coated trunk in it, the Witch Tree, is the one everybody photographs; tourist pages say 500 or 600 years, and the register will say only hundreds. At Bucaco, on the Portuguese mainland where the species does not belong at all, a til by the Lago Grande measured 38 metres tall in 2016, with a 3 metre trunk. And on Terceira in the Azores, where til was introduced, one in the parish of Terra Chã has been a tree of public interest since 1966, though no dated sighting since a 2020 Street View image has turned up.
